stem: An analyst computes a category's inventory turnover as its net sales at selling prices divided by its average stock valued at cost. Compared with dividing cost of goods sold by the same stock, what does this do?

options.text: Turnover comes out too low, because the stock includes the margin
Turnover comes out too high, because the sales include the margin
Turnover is unchanged, because price and cost cancel out in a ratio
Turnover is unchanged, because both figures cover the same year
